transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (BrightLens ML Eng), Priya Shah (BrightLens Infra), Ava Kim (BrightLens Product)

[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on for the POC weekly, throughput optim, quick agenda review, Samira will go over the latest runs and then we'll talk next steps.
[00:00:15] Samira: cool yeah so we ran the synthetic profile last night, to recap we used the short-plus-long mix you sent, 70% short prompts ~128 tokens, 30% long ~1024 tokens, batcher was configured with dynamic windowing and a 40ms hold.
[00:00:34] Carlos: sorry quick q before you jump in, is that the same warm cache settings as last week? we saw some cold-start noise in the 1st 10 minutes.
[00:00:42] Samira: good call, we added a 15min warmup before collecting metrics but yes you might still see a bit of variance on first 5-10 mins, warm cache = "KV cache" warm for common prefixes, not full model cache.
[00:01:05] Priya: jotting that down, and are you running this on the dedicated pool or hosted reference?
[00:01:10] Samira: this run was on your dedicated nodes in us-west2, the same instance types as last time (A100-equivalent), autoscaling set to min 3, max 12 pods.
[00:01:22] Ava: ok cool, what did the numbers look like?
[00:01:26] Samira: the headline: sustained 210 req/s with p50 latency around 190ms and p95 about 410ms for the mixed workload. Per-token cost increased slightly compared to last run because we pushed concurrency up to 8 per pod.
[00:01:47] Jordan: 210 req/s is promising, were those requests single-stream or were you using continuous batching?
[00:01:54] Samira: continuous batching yes, with dynamic batch size capped at 32. The batching window is adaptive but we had a hard cap at 40ms to keep latency SLOs.
[00:02:07] Carlos: hmm p95 410ms seems a hair high, we target p95 < 350ms, any obvious hotspots?
[00:02:14] Samira: looked into it — the long prompt tail drives that. When long prompts hit, "KV cache" helps a bit but sequence length dominates. Also we saw queuing spikes when concurrency per pod hit 12 total inflight requests before autoscale kicked.
[00:02:30] Jordan: ok that points to tuning concurrency and autoscale thresholds, maybe increase the target pod cpu/ gpu utilization to trigger scale earlier.
[00:02:38] Priya: our infra team is conservative on autoscale thresholds because of cost, we prefer larger pods with higher concurrency vs more pods. cost tradeoff.
[00:02:46] Samira: totally, we can model both — set target concurrency per GPU at 8 vs 12 and see cost delta. We also can change batching window to 30ms and allow slightly bigger batch sizes but that affects p50.
[00:03:00] Carlos: any observations about cache hit rates? we sent a production trace last week, did you replay that?
[00:03:06] Samira: we replayed a 15min trace, cache hit rates for prefixes were about 62% on the short prompt set, less on long. That reduced token decode by roughly 18% compared to cold runs.
[00:03:20] Jordan: great, that explains some of the gains. Another lever is quantization profile, were you on 4-bit q8 or full fp16?
[00:03:28] Samira: we ran fp16 for baseline, but we did a short q4 run — saw 1.3x throughput improvement but quality diffs on some of your longer summarization flows. We flagged that to the evals team.
[00:03:42] Ava: will the quality diffs show up in the short term? our product team needs to know tolerances.
[00:03:47] Samira: short answer, yes they can for some prompts, but we can do mixed strategy: q4 for short/fast paths and fp16 for longer sequences.
[00:03:56] Carlos: how about queueing/backpressure, when you saw concurrency spike to 12, was there request queueing at the load balancer or inside the pod?
[00:04:03] Samira: mostly internal queueing, the runtime keeps an in-flight queue per worker to batch continuously — when concurrency exceeds the per-worker limit requests get queued briefly which increases p95. The LB also has a small queue but that was negligible here.
[00:04:18] Jordan: ok so two knobs: lower per-pod concurrency to reduce internal queueing, or shorten batch window to reduce batch size variance. both impact throughput/cost.
[00:04:26] Priya: from infra side, if we lower concurrency to 8 we need more pods to keep throughput which can increase inter-pod overhead, is that a thing?
[00:04:34] Samira: slight overhead yes, but overall tokens/sec tends to be smoother; the net cost depends on your pricing model, we can run a cost model.
[00:04:42] Carlos: any immediate config you recommend we try this week?
[00:04:45] Samira: recommended starting point: concurrency 8, batch cap 32, batching window 30ms, autoscale target moved to 65% GPU util, pre-warm "KV cache" for 20 minutes prior to tests.
[00:04:58] Jordan: and we should run the 2-hour soak at 250 rps to see sustained behavior and autoscale churn.
[00:05:04] Priya: Friday works, we can carve out 2 hours 9-11am pacific.
[00:05:08] Ava: do we need to change any network or infra settings for the soak?
[00:05:11] Samira: just ensure the pod disruption budget is relaxed a bit and that the load generator uses the exact production header patterns, also we recommend turning on request-level tracing for the duration so we can correlate spikes.
[00:05:25] Carlos: about tracing, is that safe re: PII? our traces may have identifiers.
[00:05:29] Jordan: we mask PII automatically in our tracing, and we can redact client ids — Samira will send the tracing runbook.
[00:05:36] Samira: yep I'll share the runbook and the drive link to the benchmark sheet.
[00:05:40] Jordan: anything else on the bench numbers?
[00:05:43] Samira: one more thing — we noticed the GC pauses in the runtime when token decode buffers spiked; we have a patch that reduces buffer growth but it needs a quick kernel swap, low-risk, want to schedule that in a canary before the soak?
[00:05:58] Priya: yes do canary, we prefer a single pod canary during low traffic window.
[00:06:03] Jordan: ok Samira to do canary on Wednesday during off-hours, then full soak Friday.
[00:06:10] Ava: timeline sounds good. Also curious about dedicated vs hosted — we're leaning dedicated but want an apples-to-apples cost/latency comparison.
[00:06:18] Samira: we can produce a delta report; hosted has lower overhead but less network isolation, dedicated gives predictable throughput. We'll include cost model in the sheet.
[00:06:28] Carlos: one more ops ask: can you provide the pod-level metrics we saw — GPU util, inflight req, batch sizes over time — as CSV?
[00:06:36] Samira: yes CSV export will be attached to the spreadsheet.
[00:06:40] Jordan: ok wrapping up — quick recap and owners.
[00:06:44] Jordan: Samira to share benchmark sheet and runbook, Samira to run canary patch Wednesday, Samira to prepare soak script; Jordan to coordinate soak timing with Priya; Carlos to upload production trace.
[00:06:57] Carlos: got it.
[00:07:00] Priya: noted.
[00:07:02] Ava: thanks all.
[00:07:04] Samira: thanks everyone, I'll follow up with links and configs.
[00:07:08] Jordan: end.

Notes about transcript quality: some words like "KV cache" transcribed correctly, product names sometimes shortened, filler words present. There are minor mis-hearings (eg. "GC pauses" flagged as "G C pauses" in raw).
